issue: The bottom annotation 'Analytical model; no offload, latency or overlap; not measured' uses the word 'overlap' ambiguously. The plotted 1.75x factor (subtitle line 1: 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 x tensor bytes') and the prose on p.161 ('With concurrent send and receive') both assume full-duplex send/receive overlap *within* each phase, while the two phases (reduce-scatter, all-gather) are sequential. Read in isolation, 'no overlap' can be misread as negating send/receive concurrency, which would contradict the figure's own arithmetic: a half-duplex (no send/receive overlap) ring would require 3.5x M/B, not the 1.75x M/B that every curve on the plot follows. evidence: At 140 GB the NVLink marker is 544 ms = 245/450 = 1.75*140/450, a value that only holds with concurrent send+receive; all three curves are straight slope-1 lines on the log-log axes passing through 1.75*M/B with no alpha floor, confirming the model is bytes-only and full-duplex. Prose PDF 181 / printed 161 states explicitly: 'With concurrent send and receive, its ideal time is T_ring ~ 245/450 ~ 0.54 s. Equivalently, 490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time.' The figure's 'no overlap' is not reconciled with this in either the annotation or the caption.
acceptance_test: Reword the annotation so 'overlap' is unambiguous, e.g. 'Analytical model; no collective offload, no per-step latency (alpha), communication not overlapped with computation; send/receive full-duplex assumed; not measured.' correction: Rewrite as: 'Ethernet line coding differs by generation: 200GbE uses 64b/66b with FEC on two 100G lanes, while 400GbE adds a 256b/257b block-coding stage before FEC; InfiniBand HDR and NDR both use 64b/66b. Use the specific standard's payload-efficiency figure.'
